description: We are analyzing Earth changes using Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data to monitor environmental impacts.
summary:
• During major floods and earthquakes in Pakistan, cellular towers and internet infrastructure are the first to collapse, leaving rescue teams blind to real-time satellite data. SAR-Eye solves this critical last-mile gap. Inspired by the NASA-ISRO (NISAR) mission's all-weather, day-and-night Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) capabilities, SAR-Eye is a rugged, off-grid hardware receiver node deployed in high-risk zones like Islamabad. When SAR telemetry detects sudden surface water expansion or ground displacement, the node triggers immediate local visual (LED) and sensor-verified alerts without needing internet connectivity. Our prototype combines a functional Arduino-based real-time hardware simulation (Tinkercad), an engineering structural enclosure blueprint (AutoCAD), and a live telemetry alert dashboard (Canva).

NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar (NISAR) Mission Overview & Open Data Guidelines (NASA Earthdata / ASF DAAC SAR datasets).
details:
What It Does & How It Works:

SAR-Eye: Tracking Earth's Pulse is an off-grid ground receiver node designed to receive NASA-ISRO (NISAR) Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) alerts during severe floods and natural disasters. When NISAR's all-weather, day-and-night radar detects sudden surface water expansion or ground displacement, the SAR-Eye hardware node captures these telemetry alerts directly without relying on local cellular towers or internet infrastructure, triggering immediate local visual (LED) and sensor-verified warnings.

Benefits & Intended Impact:

During major floods and earthquakes in Pakistan, cellular networks and internet infrastructure are the first to collapse, leaving emergency responders blind to real-time satellite intelligence. Deployed across high-risk zones in Islamabad, Pakistan, SAR-Eye bridges this critical last-mile communication gap, enabling rescue teams and local communities to receive life-saving alerts immediately during total network blackouts.

Tools, Hardware & Software Used:

• Hardware Simulation & Embedded Logic: Tinkercad Circuits, Arduino Uno R3, MQ-2 Gas/Environmental Sensor, and C++ (Arduino IDE).

• Structural & Enclosure Design: AutoCAD (2D/3D hardware enclosure and NISAR receiver antenna mount blueprint).

• Telemetry Interface & Pitch: Canva (Live off-grid telemetry alert dashboard) and CapCut (Video demonstration).

Creativity & Key Factors Considered:

Rather than building a software-only app that fails when the internet goes down, we combined NASA's space-based SAR remote sensing with rugged, low-cost, off-grid ground hardware—considering power resilience, environmental sensor verification, and immediate local readability for first responders.
